_about: A220-100, from the Airbus A220 Aircraft Characteristics Publication (BD500-3AB48-13800-00, Issue 013-01), A220-100 General aircraft dimensions sheets 2 (side: page index 73) and 1 (plan, front: page index 72). Vector line art in a pale yellow fill (layers.py --mode strokes-in-fill), line centres. Unlike the A220-300's, these sheets aren't squeezed: one scale (the printed 34.98 m length) fits the side's height and the plan's span and width within 0.3%. The A220-300's points moved by its two plugs (plug.py), the parts this different drawing places differently re-placed. The overwing exit isn't drawn: it's placed from the door-distance figure (Figure 11, page index 100: 13.11 m to its forward edge, as the figure's other distances are to the doors' forward edges), 0.61 m wide as its outline is in the photos, as tall as the A220-300's. Cabin windows: not drawn; measured on Wikimedia Commons photos (the shape's sources).

windows.note: Measured on two side-on Wikimedia Commons photos of the left side (N124DU and N145DQ, the shape's sources), scaled between the two doors' middles: they agree within 2 cm. 12 windows from 1.31 m behind door 1's middle at a 0.537 m pitch, the exit's own window, two more 0.95 and 0.90 m apart, then 18 at about 0.533 m (two gaps of 0.57 and 0.58 m near the back) to 0.65 m ahead of the aft door; the 7 the wing hides in both photos placed at that pitch, the count from a photo of the right side where they show (HB-JBI). The band and width are the panes', the band evened out from the photos' view from below (about 9 degrees, from the doors' drawn top and bottom).

sources.title: Airbus, A220 Aircraft Characteristics Publication (BD500-3AB48-13800-00, Issue 013-01, 2026-10-29), A220-100 Aircraft description: Figure 1 General aircraft dimensions; Figure 11 Door distance from nose
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the side, plan and front views (tools/trace/bcs1/); the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The A220-100's sheets are drawn to one scale both ways; the A220-300's points were moved by its fuselage plugs (2.16 m ahead of the wing, 1.55 m behind it, from the two types' printed door and wing distances) and snapped onto them. No cabin windows drawn: they're from the photos below.

Only measurements are taken from the photo (window and door positions along the cabin, scaled between the doors' middles as the general-dimensions sheet places them); nothing of it is copied.
